messages:
anna-ops: Heads-up — we've seen a 2x increase in preemptible evictions in us-west over the last hour. A bunch of small streaming requests are failing instead of being requeued. Looking for quick mitigations we can flip before the next spike.

mohit-eng: :eyes: timeline? are these mostly short-running chat tokens or long-generation streams?

anna-ops: Mostly short streams (~300-800ms), but a noisy tail where the last chunk fails with a 502 after an eviction. Metric: evict.rate_usw = 0.9 -> 1.8 in 30m.

sarah-ml: Could be our token-lease expiry + immediate cutover. We currently issue ephemeral streaming tokens valid 60s. If the node gets preempted while a client still has an active stream, the fallback to requeue is getting rate-limited by our per-account requeue budget.

javier-runtime: Two quick low-risk knobs: 1) rotate ephemeral token lifespan to 90s for streaming endpoints (reduces mid-stream invalidation), 2) allow a tiny client-side requeue backoff with capped retries to avoid thundering herd.

mohit-eng: Agree on token TTL bump but worried about window where a stolen GPU remains running for another few seconds — we should pair TTL bump with a graceful-drain signal from node agent so clients can start local reconnect logic earlier.

anna-ops: What does graceful-drain signal look like? We need something that works with current infra and SDKs fast.

sarah-ml: Node agent can emit a short-lived header via our proxy: X-Node-Drain: true. Client SDKs already check headers on each chunk; if they see drain=true they can open a secondary connection early to the fallback pool and finish streaming there. Minimal SDK change.

javier-runtime: SDK pseudo: 
```
// on each chunk
if (resp.headers['x-node-drain'] === 'true') {
  // start background reconnect to fallback endpoint
  startReconnectToFallback();
}
```
Keep reconnect async so we don't delay successful chunks.

mohit-eng: For fallback selection: prefer cheap dedicated warm nodes over on-demand to save cost. Idea: maintain a small warm-on-demand pool in regions with high evict.rate, use a cost cap per minute to avoid runaway spend. Config example: 
```
fallback_policy: {
  preferred_pool: "warm-dedicated-usw",
  cost_cap_per_min: "$2.50"
}
```
We can flip this per-customer via rollout flag.

anna-ops: How do we prevent requeue amplification when many clients reconnect?

javier-runtime: Add a per-stream requeue budget header from control plane: X-Requeue-Budget: <n>. SDK uses it to bound retries. Also add jittered exponential backoff: base 100ms, max 2s, max_retries = min(budget,3).

sarah-ml: Also, if eviction rate > threshold, enable "soft-slo-smoothing": prefer shorter responses or trimming optional tokens for a small quality vs latency tradeoff. That reduces time-in-flight and lowers exposure window.

oncall-rota: I've scheduled a quick runbook step: if evict.rate_usw > 1.5 for 15m, flip token TTL to 90s and enable fallback_pool with cost cap. I'm adding it to the rota playbook now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: feature/evict-mitigation (anna-ops, mohit-eng) -> staging (sha: b3f2a1b) :rocket:

anna-ops: Action items: 1) mohit — rollout TTL bump + drain header feature flag gated, 2) javier — SDK small reconnect change + requeue-budget header, 3) sarah — add soft-slo-smoothing config and metrics, 4) ops — enable fallback_pool playbook step. We'll monitor evict.rate_usw and tail-5th/95th.

mohit-eng: On it, will push a staging rollout by EOD.

javier-runtime: SDK PR incoming, I'll include snippet and tests for jitter/backoff.

sarah-ml: I'll add a small eval to measure quality impact when trimming trailing tokens. Quick A/B recommended.

anna-ops: Thanks — keeping this thread as the coordination point. If anyone sees an unrelated spike, ping here. :thumbsup:
